title: Per-subtoken latency decomposition and adaptive cache-credit model
text:
Per-subtoken latency decomposition and adaptive cache-credit model

description:
Instrument per-subtoken timings across the serving runtime to decompose observed latency into model compute, KV cache lookup, kernel scheduling, and transport. Build an adaptive cache-credit model that apportions marginal cost and latency to individual subtokens when cache hits/misses change the token-level cost. The signals must feed both the billing export and latency/error dashboards in Console. Design constraints: keep tracing overhead minimal (<1% p95 latency increase for typical workloads), avoid increasing ingestion volume materially for free-tier tenants, and maintain backward compatibility with existing token traces.

acceptance_criteria:
Per-subtoken timing emitted for 99% of requests in the canary (sampling configurable)
Cache-hit delta metric computed and joined to token traces in the ingestion pipeline
Adaptive cache-credit algorithm produces per-token cost signals that align with batch-level accounting within 5% on synthetic tests
No more than 1% increase in p95 request latency observed in staging canary

implementation_notes:
Hook into existing tracing hooks at the emission boundary to record subtoken start/end timestamps and cache_result flag
Serialize timings as compact microsecond integers and attach a lightweight cache_context id for later join in aggregation
Add a new stage in the metrics ingestion pipeline to compute per-request cache delta and distribute credits to tokens using a configurable heuristic (initial heuristic: proportional to token emission compute time excluding measured cache time)
Expose token-level metrics via metrics gateway and add per-route/ per-model dashboards in Console with rollout flags

test_plan:
Unit tests for timing recorder, cache flag invariants, and serialization format
Integration test using synthetic workload with deterministic cache hit patterns to validate allocation behaviour
Load test in staging by replaying production traces to measure tracing overhead and ingestion throughput impact
E2E validation: compare aggregated per-token costs to the current billing export across 100k requests and verify drift within threshold

risks:
Tracing overhead could increase p99 for small, latency-sensitive requests if not buffered correctly
Complex batching + prefetch scenarios may cause misattribution of cache credit to the wrong token
Increased ingestion volume from token traces could stress metrics pipeline and storage costs

mitigations:
Use compact binary encoding and configurable tenant sampling (default 1% for free-tier tenants)
Provide fallback apportionment to batch-level allocation when cache semantics are ambiguous
Add ingress throttling and graceful degradation: drop token-detail under high load and emit aggregated fallback metrics

comments:
2026-03-02 - Asha Patel: Scoped initial spike to measure tracing overhead. Observed ~0.6% p95 increase with synchronous recording; plan to move to async buffering and micro-batching of trace flushes.
2026-03-04 - Miguel Ortega: Prototype implemented with compact protobuf payload for token traces. Benchmark shows a 40% reduction in payload size vs JSON. PR created for runtime hooks.
2026-03-06 - Runtime team review: Requested adding a global sequence_id to correlate token timings across batching boundaries and an explicit marker for prefetch vs on-demand cache results.
2026-03-08 - Nina Zhao (PM): Emphasized that billing-facing metrics must be conservative. If precision vs overhead is a trade-off, prefer conservative apportionment to avoid customer misbilling.
2026-03-10 - Lee Chen (Infra): Recommend gating full rollout behind KV cache v3 canary and adding ingestion backpressure behaviour to avoid pipeline overload during spikes.
2026-03-11 - Miguel Ortega: Implemented async ring buffer and batched trace flush. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2879

observability_queries:
TokenLatencyByRoute: SELECT percentile(95, latency_us) FROM token_traces WHERE route_id = ? FACET token_position
CacheDeltaByRequest: SELECT SUM(cache_miss) - SUM(cache_hit) AS cache_delta FROM cache_events FACET request_id SINCE 1 minute ago
PerTokenCostEstimate: Evaluate token_cost = base_compute_cost * (token_latency_us - cache_latency_us) + cache_credit * cache_unit_cost
